sub_problem: batch priority queue operations without full sorting

associations.structural_reason: B-trees amortize insert cost via buffered writes; batch PQ can buffer decrease-keys and process in groups
Tournament trees find min in O(1) but full sorting costs O(n log n); extracting only the top-k elements costs O(n + k log n)
Van Emde Boas layout achieves O(log_B n) amortized cost per operation by exploiting memory hierarchy; analogous to exploiting distance-hierarchy
Soft heaps allow O(1) amortized extract-min at the cost of corrupting some entries. If we tolerate approximate ordering (distances within epsilon), we can process batches faster and correct later.

associations.concept: Parallel prefix sums for batched minimum
associations.structural_reason: Prefix-min on sorted arrays finds batch minimums in O(n/B) time per batch of B elements; batched decrease-key can be structured as prefix-min on distance arrays

forced_bridges.explanation: Soft heaps provide O(1) amortized operations by allowing epsilon-corruption of min ordering. If frontier reduction allows approximate partitioning (vertices assigned to wrong distance buckets with probability epsilon), the inter-partition correction cost remains bounded while partition computation becomes O(m) instead of O(m log n).
forced_bridges.potential_insight: Use soft-heap-like corruption-tolerant partitioning in frontier reduction. Allow O(epsilon * n) vertices to be in wrong partitions, then fix them in a correction pass. If epsilon = 1/polylog(n), correction costs O(m/polylog(n)) per round.

forced_bridges.explanation: Dijkstra processes one vertex at a time. Batch processing B vertices simultaneously is analogous to parallel prefix on B processors. The 'communication cost' (inter-batch corrections) maps to prefix-sum depth O(log B).
forced_bridges.potential_insight: Process frontier in batches of B = n/log n vertices. Within each batch, relaxations proceed in parallel (no ordering needed). Inter-batch corrections need O(log B) rounds. Total comparisons: O(m + n log n / log B * log B) = O(m + n log n). Need smarter batching to break the barrier.

forced_bridges.explanation: Radix sort processes digits from least significant to most significant, achieving O(n * d) where d is the number of digits. For distances, 'digits' correspond to distance ranges at different granularities. Processing distances from coarsest to finest granularity avoids explicit sorting.
forced_bridges.potential_insight: Decompose distances into O(log log n) 'significance levels'. Process from coarsest to finest. At each level, vertices in the same bucket need only O(1) comparisons to order. Total comparisons: O(m + n log log n). But this requires distance structure knowledge — works best when distances are structured.

anomaly_results.combination: Bloom filters for distance propagation tracking
novel_associations: Track which vertices have been relaxed recently using space-efficient Bloom filters; skip re-relaxation of settled vertices without full hash table overhead
anomaly_results.emergent_insight: Approximate membership testing (Bloom filters) can accelerate the correction phase of frontier reduction by quickly identifying which vertices need re-processing.

anomaly_results.combination: Wavelet trees for priority queue operations
novel_associations: Wavelet trees support rank/select in O(log sigma) time; for a priority queue with sigma distinct priority levels, this gives O(log sigma) extract-min
anomaly_results.emergent_insight: If distances cluster into sigma << n distinct approximate levels, a wavelet-tree-based PQ achieves O(log sigma) per operation instead of O(log n).

steering_directions.rationale: Soft heaps allow O(1) amortized operations with bounded corruption. Using them for frontier partitioning reduces the per-level cost from O(m log n) to O(m), at the cost of O(epsilon*n) misclassified vertices per level.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement a soft heap and measure the corruption rate on shortest-path distance distributions from the benchmark graphs.

steering_directions.direction: Adaptive batch sizes based on local graph structure
steering_directions.rationale: Uniform batching doesn't exploit structural variation. Regions with low effective diameter (expander-like) can use large batches; high-diameter regions need small batches.
steering_directions.first_step: Compute the local expansion profile of benchmark graphs and correlate with optimal batch size.

steering_directions.direction: Hierarchical distance bucketing with lazy refinement
steering_directions.rationale: Like radix sort processing digits, process distances at decreasing granularity. Initial coarse buckets computed in O(m) time; refine only buckets that affect the shortest-path DAG structure.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement a 2-level bucket system: coarse buckets of width Delta, fine buckets within each coarse bucket. Measure how many fine-bucket operations are needed.
